title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (2nd part of the Longue Marche sequel). Grothendieck fixes two elements rho, sigma of a set 𝔖 of 'twisted' elements acting on a profinite group Ĝ, written Ĉ on the previous page. They are best read as elements of a semidirect product or of Aut(Ĝ), e.g. the generators of order 2 and 3 in the PSL2(Z)/cartographic setting. He studies automorphisms u that send rho and sigma to conjugates of themselves, twisted by cocycle-like factors, which is the setting in which the GT-type 'loop equations' live.

The groups involved:
- B_{rho,sigma}: the relevant group of such u.
- Z_rho, Z_sigma: centralizers in a big group; SZ_rho = Cent_Ĉ(rho) and SZ_sigma = Cent_Ĉ(sigma) are their parts in Ĉ.
- G_{rho,sigma}: a further auxiliary group.
- Γ_{rho,sigma}: an 'outer' quotient. All the groups above are extensions of Γ_{rho,sigma} by inner parts.

Previous page:
- (56) writes M°_{rho,sigma} as an iterated fibre product Z_rho ×_Γ Z_sigma ×_Γ G_{rho,sigma}.
- (57) gives the exact sequence 1 → SZ_rho × SZ_sigma × Ĉ → M° → Γ → 1.
- (51) embeds Ĉ as the third factor, u ↦ (1,1,u).

This page:
- (52) 1 → Ĝ → M°_{rho,sigma} → Γ°_{rho,sigma} → 1. Here Γ° is the quotient by the third-factor copy of Ĝ; Grothendieck queries in the margin whether the quotient should rather be SG_{rho,sigma}.
- (53) the analogous sequence 1 → Ĝ → S_0M° → S_0Γ° → 1, deduced via (49)/(50).
- (53') marginal sequence 1 → SZ_rho × SZ_sigma → M° → G → 1, projecting onto the third factor.
- (54) Map S_0M° → Ĝ³, {u,a,b,U} ↦ (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}, uU^{-1}) = (α, β, f). These are well defined because u, a, b, U have the same image in Γ, so the 'differences' are inner, i.e. lie in Ĝ.
- (55) By a corollary on p. 557 (cf. (37)) this map induces a bijection S_0M° ≅ SG_{rho,sigma} × Ĝ. So, up to the free normalising factor f, S_0M° is parametrised by the solution set SG_{rho,sigma} of the twisted equations.
- (56)–(57) Dictionary between the quadruple (u, a, b, U) in B, Z_rho, Z_sigma, G and the derived elements α, β, f, ξ, η, α0, β0, g, h of Ĝ.
- (58) Definitions:
  - ξ = α rho(α)^{-1} and η = β sigma(β)^{-1}: coboundary-type twists measuring how u moves rho and sigma.
  - α0 = f^{-1}α and β0 = f^{-1}β.
  - g = α0 rho(α0)^{-1} = f^{-1} ξ rho(f) and h = f^{-1} η sigma(f): the same twists after normalising by f.
- The next page gives u(rho) = int(f^{-1})(ξ rho) and u(sigma) = int(f^{-1})(η sigma). It also notes that only part b) of the 'fundamental hypothesis' was used, and introduces the effective pairs Σ^eff and SG^eff.

Overall this is routine bookkeeping of extensions and fibre products. Its aim is to parametrise a group of automorphisms preserving the conjugacy classes of two given elements by explicit solutions (α, β, f) of twisted cocycle equations, as groundwork for the 'loop equation' (GT-type) analysis.
errors: In (58) the image reads 'α0 = f^{-1}α f', but consistency with g = α0 rho(α0)^{-1} = f^{-1} ξ rho(f) and with β0 = f^{-1}β requires α0 = f^{-1}α. The trailing 'f' is a slip or a stray comma.

(52) is stated with kernel Ĝ and quotient Γ°, whereas (57) on the previous page has kernel SZ_rho × SZ_sigma × Ĉ over Γ. (52) is only correct if Γ° denotes the quotient of M° by the third-factor copy of Ĝ, not Γ_{rho,sigma} itself. Grothendieck himself hesitates ('peut-être plutôt SG_{rho,sigma}?') and adds the alternative sequence (53').
(55) is a bijection of sets deduced from p. 557; whether it is a group isomorphism is not claimed. The group structure on SG × Ĝ would be twisted, not the plain product.

ideas.what: Describing groups of automorphisms that fix conjugacy classes of two elements via iterated fibre products of centralizers over an outer group Γ, with exact sequences relating them
ideas.modern_name: Fibre products of group extensions / outer automorphism groups preserving conjugacy classes (braid-like or GT-like automorphism groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; GT context: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Parametrisation of automorphisms by elements (α, β, f) of the profinite group satisfying twisted coboundary relations ξ = α rho(α)^{-1}, with u(rho) = int(f^{-1})(ξ rho)
ideas.modern_name: Twisted cocycle / nonabelian H^1 description of the GT-type loop equations (e.g. Lochak–Schneps involution/order-3 relations)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of extensions and a change of variables in an ongoing computation. There is no standalone result or new connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top line reads 'dont l'image est la troisième facteur dans la ... de (57)' (facteur, not 'fonction').
In (58) the image shows 'α0 = f^{-1}α f' with a trailing f, mathematically intended as α0 = f^{-1}α.
The marginal (53') is written vertically in the left margin: 1 → SZ_rho × SZ_sigma → M°_{rho,sigma} → G → 1.
The quantities in (56) carry membership marks: u ∈ B_{rho,sigma}, a ∈ Z_rho, b ∈ Z_sigma, U ∈ G_{rho,sigma}. The transcription's 'P̂' should be B.
